In the Kitchen with Lili

Lili's Kitchen — My Recipe Book
📖 122 recipes🌍 9 cuisines📸 process photos💗 like✅ done

Welcome to my recipe book. It began with one week's menu in Lisbon — and grew into a trip around the world: Portugal, Mozambique, Brazil, Italy, South Africa, Mexico, Japan, India and the United States. Every recipe has a photo of how it should look, process photos with the why behind each phase, honest times, ingredients you can check off and a calm guided step-by-step. Mark each recipe as done ✅ when you cook it and like 💗 your favorites — they are saved on their own pages for later.

by Lili Pessane

Monday · Soups

Roasted Pumpkin Cream Soup

Creme de abóbora assada
Prep10 min
Cooking35 min
Total45 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Orange, creamy soup with a hint of sweetness — roasting the pumpkin makes all the difference.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 800 g pumpkin, cut into cubes
  • 1 onion, cut into quarters
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 700 ml vegetable stock or hot water
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 100 ml heavy cream (optional)
  • salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Preheat the oven to 200°C.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Put the pumpkin, onion and garlic on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, salt and pepper.
  3. Roast for 25 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
  4. Move everything to a pot, add the stock and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
  5. Blend with an immersion blender until you have a smooth cream.
  6. Add the cream and nutmeg, taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot, with a drizzle of olive oil on top.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Garlic toastToasted pumpkin seedsCrunchy croutonsA little grated cheese on top
Lili's tipRoasting the pumpkin before cooking it is the trick: it gets a sweet, toasted flavor that plain boiled soup doesn't have.

Monday · Meat

Oven-Roasted Chicken Legs with Carrot Rice

Pernas de frango assadas no forno com arroz de cenoura
Prep15 min
Cooking45 min
Total60 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Crispy skin, juicy chicken, and fluffy orange rice on the side.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 4 chicken legs
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 0,5 lemon (the juice)
  • 300 g rice
  • 2 grated carrots
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 600 ml hot water
  • 1 leaf bay leaf
  • salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the chicken with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Let it pick up flavor for 10 minutes.
  2. Oven at 200°C: roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning halfway. It's ready when the skin is golden and crispy.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In a pot, sauté the onion and garlic in a drizzle of olive oil for 3 minutes. Add the grated carrot and stir for 2 more minutes.
  4. Add the rice, stir for 1 minute, then add the hot water, bay leaf and salt.
  5. Cover and cook over low heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve with the chicken on top and a slice of lemon.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Simple green saladRoasted vegetablesYogurt sauce with garlic and lemonMild piri-piri, for those who like it
Lili's tipIf you have time, season the chicken in the morning and keep it in the fridge. By dinner the flavor is much better.

Couscous with Roasted Vegetables & Dried Fruit

Couscous de legumes assados e frutos secos
Prep10 min
Cooking15 min
Total25 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Light, colorful and quick: fluffy couscous with sweet vegetables and a touch of dried fruit.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 250 g couscous
  • 250 ml hot stock
  • 1 zucchini, cut into cubes
  • 1 red bell pepper, cut into cubes
  • 1 carrot, cut into small cubes
  • 1 red onion
  • 50 g dried fruit (raisins and chopped apricot)
  • 40 g almonds or chopped walnuts
  • 1 tsp cumin
  • 0,5 lemon (the juice)
  • olive oil, salt, pepper and cilantro or mint

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sauté or roast the vegetables in olive oil for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden. Season with salt, pepper and cumin.
  2. Boil the stock and pour it over the couscous in a bowl. Cover and wait 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Fluff the couscous with a fork and add a drizzle of olive oil.
  4. Mix in the vegetables, dried fruit and almonds.
  5. Add the lemon juice and chopped herbs. Taste and adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  6. Serve warm — it's great freshly made and the next day too.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Grilled chicken on the sideBaked salmonTomato saladYogurt sauce with mint
Lili's tipDon't cook couscous like pasta. You just hydrate it with hot stock, covered — otherwise it turns to mush.

Portuguese Kale Soup

Caldo verde
Prep10 min
Cooking25 min
Total35 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

The Portuguese classic: a potato cream with very finely cut kale and a drizzle of olive oil.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 g potatoes, cut into cubes
  • 1 onion
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 200 g very finely sliced Galician kale (or kale)
  • 1200 ml water
  • 4 slices chorizo (optional)
  • olive oil and salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the potatoes, onion and garlic in salted water for 20 minutes.
  2. Blend everything until you have a smooth cream. If it's too thick, add a little more hot water.
  3. Put it back on the heat. When it boils, add the very finely cut kale.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Cook only 5 to 7 minutes — the kale should stay bright green and tender, not brown.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  5. Add a good drizzle of olive oil and adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  6. Serve piping hot, with a slice of chorizo on top of each bowl.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Corn bread (broa)Homemade bread for dipping in the soupA drizzle of good olive oil on top
Lili's tipCut the kale as thin as you can. And don't overcook it: it loses its color and flavor.

Hake Fillets with Russian Salad

Filetes de pescada com salada russa
Prep20 min
Cooking15 min
Total35 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Breaded, golden fish with that creamy salad of potato, carrot and peas.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 4 hake fillets
  • 100 g flour
  • 1 beaten egg
  • 100 g breadcrumbs
  • 3 potatoes, cut into cubes
  • 2 carrots, cut into cubes
  • 150 g peas
  • 3 tbsp mayonnaise
  • 0,5 lemon
  • olive oil, salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the potato, carrot and peas in salted water. Drain and let cool.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Mix the vegetables with the mayonnaise, a few drops of lemon and pepper. Keep in the fridge.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  3. Season the fillets with salt, pepper and lemon. Coat each one in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
  4. Heat olive oil in a skillet and fry for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until golden. (In the oven: 200°C, 15 minutes.)
  5. Rest the fillets on paper towels for a minute, to drain the extra oil.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Serve with the nice and cold Russian salad and lemon slices.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green saladFluffy white riceOven potatoes instead of fried
Lili's tipRussian salad made the day before tastes even better — the flavors come together in the fridge.

Gluten-Free Penne with Vegetables & Almond

Penne sem glúten com legumes e amêndoa
Prep10 min
Cooking15 min
Total25 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Quick pasta with sautéed vegetables and crunchy toasted almond on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 320 g gluten-free penne
  • 1 zucchini, cut into half-moons
  • 1 bell pepper, cut into strips
  • 150 g cherry tomatoes, cut in half
  • 2 cloves sliced garlic
  • 40 g sliced almonds
  • olive oil, salt, pepper and basil
  • grated Parmesan cheese (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the pasta in well-salted water, for the time on the package. Save a cup of the cooking water.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. In a dry skillet, toast the almonds for 2 minutes until fragrant. Remove and set aside.
  3. In the same skillet, sauté the garlic and vegetables in olive oil for 6 to 7 minutes. The tomato goes in at the end.
  4. Add the drained pasta and a little of the cooking water. Stir well, 1 minute.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  5. Turn off the heat. Add the basil and Parmesan.
  6. Serve with the toasted almonds on top — they're what gives the crunch.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Arugula saladGrilled chicken on the sideCrumbled feta cheese on top
Lili's tipThe cooking water has starch and it binds the pasta to the vegetables. Don't throw it away!

Vegetable Cream Soup

Creme de legumes
Prep10 min
Cooking25 min
Total35 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

The everyday soup: simple, light and great for using up the vegetables you have at home.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 2 potatoes
  • 2 carrots
  • 1 zucchini
  • 1 onion
  • 1 leek
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 900 ml stock or hot water
  • olive oil, salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cut all the vegetables into pieces of about the same size.
  2. Sauté the onion, leek and garlic in olive oil for 3 minutes.
  3. Add the other vegetables and the stock. Cook for 20 minutes, until everything is soft.
  4. Blend until you have a smooth cream. Add hot water if it's too thick.
  5. Taste, adjust the salt, and serve with a drizzle of olive oil.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

🍽️ What to serve it with

ToastCroutonsChopped hard-boiled egg on top

Serves4 people

Layers of pasta, meat with tomato and béchamel, with golden cheese on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 12 sheets lasagna noodles
  • 500 g ground beef
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 400 g crushed tomato
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 500 ml béchamel (store-bought or homemade)
  • 100 g grated cheese
  • olive oil, salt, pepper, oregano and nutmeg

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil. Add the meat and let it brown well, stirring to break it up.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Add the tomato, paste, oregano, salt and pepper. Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  3. If you make the béchamel at home: melt 50 g of butter, add 50 g of flour, then 500 ml of milk a little at a time, always stirring until it thickens. Season with salt and nutmeg.
  4. In a baking dish, build layers: a little béchamel, pasta sheets, meat, béchamel. Repeat 3 times.
  5. Finish with béchamel and the grated cheese over everything.
  6. Oven at 180°C for 30 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting — it slices much better.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A very simple green saladGarlic breadGrilled vegetables on the side
Lili's tipThe rest at the end is not optional: it's what makes the slices come out neat instead of falling apart.

Serves4 people

Portugal's most famous oven rice: shredded duck, a crispy top and chorizo over it all.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g duck (half a duck or legs)
  • 300 g short-grain rice (arroz carolino)
  • 1 onion
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 1 leaf bay leaf
  • 100 g chorizo, cut into slices
  • 900 ml water (to cook the duck — save the broth)
  • olive oil, salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the duck in water with salt, bay leaf and half the onion for 40 minutes, until very tender. Save the broth — it's gold.
  2. Remove the duck, let it cool a little, shred the meat and take off skin and bones.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  3. Sauté the other half of the onion and the garlic in olive oil. Add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
  4. Add the duck broth (twice the volume of the rice) and cook for 12 to 15 minutes.
  5. Mix the shredded duck into the rice and move everything to an oven dish.
  6. Put the chorizo slices on top and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, until the top is crispy and golden.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green salad with orangeRoasted vegetablesA simple tomato salad
Lili's tipThe crispy top is this dish's signature. Don't skip the oven step at the end.

Cooking35 min
Total50 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Whole fish in the oven with that vinegary onion and pepper sauce poured over the top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 2 whole cleaned sea breams (or 4 fillets)
  • 3 potatoes, cut into slices
  • 1 onion, cut into slices
  • 1 bell pepper, cut into strips
  • 2 cloves sliced garlic
  • 100 ml white wine vinegar
  • 100 ml olive oil
  • 1 leaf bay leaf
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • salt, pepper, lemon and chopped parsley

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Oven at 200°C. Put the potatoes on a tray with olive oil and salt and roast for 20 minutes, to give them a head start.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Season the fish with salt and lemon, place it over the potatoes and roast for 15 to 18 more minutes.
  3. Meanwhile make the escabeche: heat the olive oil and soften the onion, pepper, garlic and bay leaf, without letting it burn.
  4. Add the paprika and vinegar, let it boil for 1 to 2 minutes and turn off the heat.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Pour the hot escabeche over the roasted fish.
  6. Let it rest for 5 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the potatoes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Tomato saladSautéed broccoli or greensWhite rice on the side
Lili's tipThe escabeche should go over the fish hot — that contrast is what makes it special. The next day, cold, it's great too.

Serves 4 people

Spaghetti Carbonara

Prep10 min
Cooking15 min

Serves4 people

The Roman classic: creamy pasta with egg and cheese, no cream — the trick is in the technique.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 320 g spaghetti
  • 150 g guanciale or pancetta (or bacon), cut into strips
  • 3 egg yolks
  • 1 whole egg
  • 60 g pecorino or Parmesan cheese, finely grated
  • freshly ground black pepper and salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water. Save a cup of the cooking water — you'll need it.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Fry the guanciale in a large skillet, with no oil, until golden and crispy. Turn off the heat.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In a bowl, beat the yolks, the egg, the cheese and plenty of pepper. It becomes a thick paste.
  4. Drain the pasta and add it to the skillet, off the heat.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  5. Add the egg mixture and a little of the cooking water. Stir fast — the heat of the pasta makes a creamy sauce, without cooking the egg.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  6. Serve right away, with more cheese and pepper on top.

Lili's tipOff the heat, always. If the skillet is boiling, the egg turns into an omelet — and carbonara should be creamy.

  • 1200 ml hot vegetable stock
  • 100 ml white wine (or more stock)
  • 40 g butter
  • 50 g grated Parmesan
  • olive oil, salt, pepper and parsley

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sauté the mushrooms in very hot olive oil until golden. Set aside.
  2. In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil and a little butter, for 3 minutes.
  3. Add the rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the grains look shiny.
  4. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, stirring.
  5. Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, always stirring. Only add the next one when the previous is absorbed. It takes about 18 minutes.
  6. When the rice is soft but still has a little bite in the middle, turn off the heat. Add the butter, Parmesan and mushrooms. Cover for 2 minutes and serve right away.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Arugula salad with lemonGrilled chicken on the sideA drizzle of truffle oil, for special days
Lili's tipRisotto waits for no one: serve it as soon as it's ready, or it keeps thickening in the pot.

Tomato & Basil Bruschetta

Bruschetta de tomate e manjericão
Prep10 min
Cooking5 min
Total15 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Toasted bread, ripe tomato, basil and good olive oil. Italy's simplest starter.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 4 thick slices rustic bread
  • 4 ripe tomatoes, cut into cubes
  • 1 clove garlic, cut in half
  • 8 leaves basil
  • 3 tbsp good olive oil
  • salt and pepper
  • balsamic vinegar (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Put the tomato in a bowl with salt and let it rest for 10 minutes — the salt draws out the juice and concentrates the flavor.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  2. Drain the tomato, add the olive oil, pepper and the basil torn by hand.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  3. Toast the bread until golden and crunchy.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Rub the cut side of the garlic on the still-warm bread. It smells good right away.
  5. Spoon the tomato over the bread.
  6. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil (and a few drops of balsamic, if you like) and serve right away.

🍽️ What to serve it with

As a starter, before a pastaWith a soup, it makes a light mealAlongside a caprese salad
Lili's tipDo everything at the last minute: if the tomato sits on the bread, the bread goes soggy — and bruschetta should be crunchy.

Chicken Cacciatore

Cooking40 min
Total55 min

Serves4 people

Chicken cooked slowly in a tomato, pepper and olive sauce, hunter style.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 800 g chicken thighs and legs
  • 1 onion, cut into slices
  • 1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 400 g crushed tomato
  • 100 ml red wine or stock
  • 80 g olives
  • olive oil, salt, pepper, oregano and parsley

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it in olive oil, 4 minutes on each side. Set aside.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. In the same pot, sauté the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic at the end.
  3. Pour in the wine (or stock) and scrape the bottom of the pot — that's where the flavor is.
  4. Add the tomato, oregano and olives. Put the chicken back in.
  5. Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened a bit.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  6. Sprinkle with parsley and serve very hot.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White riceShort pastaRustic bread for the sauceMashed potatoes
Lili's tipThis sauce tastes even better the next day. Make extra and save a meal.

Tiramisu

Tiramisù
Prep25 min
Cooking0 min
Total25 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

Layers of ladyfingers soaked in coffee and a light mascarpone cream. No oven.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 250 g mascarpone cheese
  • 200 ml heavy cream, very cold, for whipping
  • 3 eggs (yolks and whites separated)
  • 80 g sugar
  • 200 g ladyfinger cookies
  • 250 ml strong coffee, already cold
  • cocoa powder, for dusting

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Beat the yolks with the sugar until you have a pale, fluffy cream.
  2. Add the mascarpone and stir until combined, without overbeating.
  3. Whip the cream until firm and fold it into the cream. Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in too, gently.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Dip each ladyfinger in the coffee — quickly, just get it wet, or it falls apart.
  5. Build layers in a dish: ladyfingers, cream, ladyfingers, cream.
  6. Keep in the fridge for at least 4 hours (overnight is ideal). Dust with cocoa before serving.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

🍽️ What to serve it with

An espresso on the sideAfter a pasta dinnerRed berries on top, for a fresh touch
Lili's tipYou don't eat tiramisu the same day you make it — it needs hours in the fridge to set and gain flavor.

Portuguese Salt Cod Fritters

Cooking20 min
Total40 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Golden, fluffy little cakes of cod and potato — also called bolinhos in the north.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 300 g soaked salt cod
  • 300 g potatoes
  • 1 very finely chopped onion
  • 2 eggs
  • chopped parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg
  • oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the potatoes and the cod. Drain both very well — this step is very important.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  2. Mash the potatoes while still hot and shred the cod very finely, with no bones.
  3. Mix the cod, the mash, onion, parsley and seasonings. Add the eggs one at a time, until you have a mixture you can shape.
  4. With two wet spoons, shape little cakes about the size of a small egg.
  5. Fry in hot oil until golden all over. Drain on paper towels.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  6. Serve warm or at room temperature — cold they're good too, on a picnic.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Tomato riceLettuce and onion saladAs a snack, with a beer or a very fresh juice
Lili's tipThe mixture has to be very dry. If the cod or potato holds too much water, the fritters burst open in the oil.

Serves 2 people

  • 2 thin beef steaks

Make the sauce: boil the beer with the tomato and stock for 10 minutes, season with piri-piri to taste, until you have a smooth, velvety sauce.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. Portuguese Custard Tart

Pastel de nata
Prep25 min
Cooking20 min
Total45 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

Crispy puff pastry and a cinnamon egg custard. Warm, fresh out of the oven, it's something else.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 1 roll puff pastry
  • 250 ml milk
  • 150 g sugar
  • 3 tbsp flour
  • 4 egg yolks
  • 1 stick cinnamon and 1 lemon peel
  • ground cinnamon and powdered sugar, for serving

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Bring the milk to a simmer with the cinnamon and lemon until almost boiling. Remove from the heat.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Mix the sugar with the flour and add a little of the hot milk, stirring. Then add it all back to the milk and cook, always stirring, until it thickens like a cream.
  3. Remove from the heat, let it cool for 5 minutes and add the yolks one at a time, stirring fast.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  4. Roll out the puff pastry, roll it up like a log, cut slices and line muffin tins, spreading the pastry with wet thumbs.
  5. Fill the tins up to 3/4 with the custard.
  6. A very hot oven, 250°C, for 12 to 15 minutes, until the custard gets those toasted little spots. Serve warm, with cinnamon.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A coffee (a 'bica', as they say in Lisbon)On their own, still warmWith a scoop of vanilla ice cream
Lili's tipThe oven at maximum is the secret of the toasted spots. No fear: that's really how they are.

Matapa com arroz

Cooking45 min
Total60 min

Serves4 people

Mozambique's soul dish: cassava leaves in a peanut and coconut sauce.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 g pounded cassava leaves (matapa; or very finely chopped spinach)
  • 400 ml coconut milk
  • 150 g ground peanut (or natural peanut butter)
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 200 g shrimp (optional, for the party version)
  • salt and a little hot water
  • 300 g rice, on the side

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. If you use fresh leaves, pound or chop them very finely. Nowadays they're sold already pounded and frozen — it saves a lot of work.
  2. Boil the leaves in salted water for 20 minutes, to remove the bitterness. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Sauté the onion and garlic. Add the drained leaves.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  4. Add the coconut milk and ground peanut, a little at a time, stirring so it doesn't stick.
  5. Cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is creamy and combined.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  6. If you make the shrimp version, add it in the last 5 minutes. Serve over fluffy white rice.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White rice (the classic)Xima, for the more traditional versionPrawn curry on the side, on a party day
Lili's tipGood matapa is creamy, with no lumps of peanut. Stir calmly and add the peanut a little at a time.

Mozambican Piri-Piri Chicken

Frango piri-piri

Cooking35 min

Serves4 people

Chicken marinated and grilled with the piri-piri sauce that was born in Mozambique.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 1 whole chicken, butterflied (or 4 large legs)
  • 4 cloves crushed garlic
  • 2 piri-piri chilies (or to taste)
  • 1 lemon (the juice)
  • 3 tbsp olive oil or oil
  • 1 tsp paprika
  • salt, pepper and extra piri-piri sauce for serving

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Make the marinade: mix the garlic, chopped piri-piri, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, salt and pepper.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Rub the chicken well on all sides. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes — overnight is even better.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  3. Heat the grill well, or the oven to 200°C.
  4. Grill/roast the chicken for 30 to 35 minutes, turning and brushing with the marinade, until nicely golden with toasted skin at the edges.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  5. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Serve with extra piri-piri sauce on the side — everyone adds the heat they can handle.

🍽️ What to serve it with

FriesCoconut riceA simple saladBread for the sauce
Lili's tipHeat is built up: start with little piri-piri in the marinade and serve extra sauce on the side. Taking heat away is what you can't do.

Cassava & Coconut Cake

Prep15 min
Cooking45 min
Total60 min

Serves6 people

A moist, dense cake of grated cassava and coconut — a homemade snack, in Mozambique and in Brazil.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 500 g raw cassava, finely grated
  • 200 g sugar
  • 200 ml coconut milk
  • 100 g shredded coconut
  • 2 eggs
  • 50 g melted butter
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • a pinch of salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a pan with butter and flour.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Mix the grated cassava with the sugar, shredded coconut and salt.

  5. Pour into the pan and smooth the top.
  6. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out almost clean. Let it cool before cutting — it slices much better warm/cold.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

A nice hot teaAfternoon coffeeOn its own, as a snack — like it always was

Brazilian Feijoada — Black Bean Stew

Feijoada brasileira
Prep20 min
Cooking90 min
Total110 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

Black beans cooked slowly with meats, served with everything it deserves.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 500 g black beans, soaked overnight
  • 300 g pork, cut into cubes (ribs or shoulder)
  • 200 g linguiça sausage, cut into slices
  • 150 g bacon, cut into cubes
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 3 cloves minced garlic
  • 2 leaves bay leaves
  • salt, pepper and oil

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the soaked beans in fresh water with the bay leaves, over low heat, for 40 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  2. Separately, brown the meats and sausage in a skillet. That browning is what gives feijoada its flavor.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Add the browned meats to the beans.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Sauté the onion, garlic and bacon and add that too, fat and all.
  5. Cook everything together for 40 to 50 more minutes, until the beans are soft and the broth is thick. Add hot water if it dries out.
  6. Adjust the salt at the end (the meats already bring salt). Serve very hot, with the sides alongside.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White riceKale cut very thin and sautéed with garlicOrange slices (they help digestion, they say — and it's true that they're refreshing)Farofa sprinkled on top
Lili's tipFeijoada is Saturday food, made calmly. Don't rush: low heat and time make the broth.

Brazilian Cheese Bread

Pão de queijo
Prep15 min
Cooking25 min
Total40 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

Gluten-free little cheese rolls, crispy outside and stretchy inside. From Minas Gerais to the world.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 250 g sweet tapioca starch (polvilho doce)
  • 120 ml milk
  • 60 ml oil
  • 1 egg
  • 150 g grated aged cheese (Parmesan or well-grated island cheese)
  • 0,5 tsp salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil the milk with the oil and salt.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Pour that hot mixture over the tapioca starch and stir with a spoon — it becomes a sticky dough, that's normal. Let it cool a little.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  3. Add the egg and knead with your hands.
  4. Add the grated cheese and knead until it comes together.
  5. Make little balls the size of a walnut, with oil-greased hands.
  6. Oven at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes, until they puff up and turn golden. Eat them warm — that's when they're at their best.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Coffee (the classic pairing in Minas)Requeijão or dulce de leche to spreadAs a snack, any time
Lili's tipThe dough is sticky and strange before the cheese. Trust it: once baked, they turn out light and stretchy.

Brazilian Fish Stew — Moqueca

Moqueca de peixe
Prep15 min
Cooking25 min
Total40 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Fish cooked in coconut milk, tomato and peppers, fragrant with cilantro. From Bahia.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g thick steaks or fillets of white fish
  • 1 onion, cut into rings
  • 1 bell pepper, cut into rings
  • 2 tomatoes, cut into slices
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 200 ml coconut milk
  • olive oil (and dendê palm oil, if you have it, 1 spoonful), salt, lemon and cilantro

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the fish with salt, garlic and lemon juice. Let it sit for 10 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  2. In a wide pot, build layers: onion, pepper, tomato, fish — and repeat.
  3. Drizzle with the coconut milk and a thread of olive oil (and the dendê, if using — it's what gives the orange color).
  4. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, without stirring with a spoon — shake the pot, so the fish doesn't fall apart.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Uncover, add chopped cilantro and let it cook down for 3 minutes uncovered.
  6. Serve right away, with the sauce over the fish.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Fluffy white riceFarofaPirão (the sauce thickened with cassava flour)
Lili's tipMoqueca isn't stirred, it's shaken. Fish is fragile, and nice pieces are part of the dish.

Brazilian Chicken Coxinha

Coxinha de frango
Prep40 min
Cooking20 min
Total60 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

Brazil's most loved snack: soft dough, shredded chicken and that little teardrop shape.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 300 g cooked, shredded chicken breast (save the broth)
  • 500 ml chicken broth
  • 250 g wheat flour
  • 1 very finely chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • parsley, salt, pepper and paprika (colorau)
  • milk and breadcrumbs, for coating; oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sauté the onion and garlic, add the shredded chicken, paprika, salt, pepper and parsley. This is the filling — taste it, it should be well seasoned.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  2. Boil the broth with a drizzle of oil and salt. Add the flour all at once and stir hard until it forms a ball of dough that comes away from the pot.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  3. Move the dough to the counter and knead it while warm until smooth. Let it cool, covered.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  4. Take pieces of dough, open a disc in your hand, put filling in the middle and close it pulling a little tip upward — the teardrop shape (or little chicken thigh!).
  5. Coat in milk and breadcrumbs.
  6. Fry in hot oil until golden. Drain and serve hot.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Mild pepper sauceKetchup and mayonnaise, like at the snack barsAs a party snack, with very cold juices
Lili's tipThe dough cooks in the pot before shaping — that's what makes it soft instead of raw inside after frying.

Brazilian Brigadeiro Fudge Balls

Brigadeiro
Prep5 min
Cooking15 min
Total20 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

The little sweet at every Brazilian party: condensed milk and chocolate, rolled in sprinkles.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 1 can sweetened condensed milk (395 g)
  • 3 tbsp cocoa or chocolate powder
  • 1 tbsp butter (and a little more for greasing your hands)
  • chocolate sprinkles, for rolling

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Put the condensed milk, cocoa and butter in a heavy-bottomed pot.
  2. Cook over medium-low heat, always stirring with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  3. It's ready when, tilting the pot, the mixture pulls away from the bottom all at once ('brigadeiro point').
  4. Pour it onto a greased plate and let it cool completely.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  5. Grease your hands with butter, roll little balls and roll them in the sprinkles.
  6. Put them in paper cups. If there are leftovers — which is rare — keep them in the fridge.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

🍽️ What to serve it with

At parties, with other little sweetsWith a coffeeStraight from the spoon, still in the pot (the 'brigadeiro de colher' version)
Lili's tipDon't stop stirring or turn up the heat to hurry: it burns on the bottom in seconds and the flavor is ruined.

American Mac & Cheese

Mac and cheese
Prep10 min
Cooking20 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

America's most famous comfort dish: pasta in a really creamy cheese sauce.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 300 g short pasta (elbow macaroni or another short shape)
  • 50 g butter
  • 40 g flour
  • 600 ml milk
  • 250 g shredded cheddar cheese
  • 1 tsp mustard (the flavor trick)
  • salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the pasta in salted water, 1 minute less than the package says. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  2. Melt the butter, add the flour, and cook for 1 minute, stirring — this is the roux, the base of the sauce.
  3. Add the milk a little at a time, stirring constantly, and cook until it thickens, about 5 minutes.
  4. Take it off the heat. Add the mustard and the cheese by the handful, stirring until melted. Don't boil it again, or the cheese will turn grainy.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss well.
  6. Serve right away, piping hot and melty. (Oven version: bake for 10 minutes with breadcrumbs on top until golden.)

🍽️ What to serve it with

A green salad, for balanceBroccoli or peas on the sideWith roast chicken, American style
Lili's tipThe sauce comes off the heat when the cheese goes in. That's the difference between creamy and grainy.

Classic American Cheeseburger

Hambúrguer americano clássico
Prep10 min
Cooking10 min
Total20 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

The original: well-seasoned beef, melting cheese, and a butter-toasted bun.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 g ground beef (with some fat — 80/20 is ideal)
  • 4 burger buns
  • 4 slices cheddar or American cheese
  • lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles
  • mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard; salt and pepper; butter for the buns

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Divide the beef into 4 balls and flatten them into patties a little wider than the buns (they shrink). Press a small dent in the center with your thumb.
  2. Season only with salt and pepper, on the outside, right when you're about to grill.
  3. Very hot grill or skillet: 3 to 4 minutes per side. Don't press the burger — all the juice runs out.
  4. In the last minute, put the cheese on top and cover, so it melts.
  5. Toast the cut buns in a skillet with a little butter.
  6. Build it: sauces on the bun, lettuce, tomato, the cheesy patty, onion, and pickles. Serve right away.

🍽️ What to serve it with

French friesColeslawFried onion ringsA milkshake, for the full menu
Lili's tipThe dent in the middle isn't a quirk: it keeps the burger from puffing up into a ball instead of a disc.

American Corn Chowder

Sopa cremosa de milho e batata
Prep15 min
Cooking30 min
Total45 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

A really creamy chowder, with sweet corn, potato, and a smoky touch from the bacon.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 400 g corn (fresh, frozen, or canned and drained)
  • 2 potatoes, cut into small cubes
  • 100 g bacon, cut into small cubes
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves minced garlic
  • 700 ml chicken or vegetable broth
  • 200 ml heavy cream or whole milk
  • salt, pepper, thyme, and chives

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Fry the bacon in a pot until crispy. Take it out and set it aside, leaving the fat in the pot.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Sauté the onion in that fat (or in olive oil) for 4 minutes. Add the garlic.
  3. Add the potato and the broth. Cook for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
  4. Add the corn and cook 5 more minutes.
  5. Blend one third of the soup (or mash some of the potato with a fork) — that's what makes it creamy without needing lots of cream.
  6. Add the cream, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve with the crispy bacon and chives on top.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Toast or saltine crackers, like in the USA green saladOn its own, as a light winter meal
Lili's tipBlending only one third is the chowder trick: creamy, but still with chunks to chew.

American BBQ Ribs

Costelinhas com molho barbecue
Prep15 min
Cooking150 min
Total165 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Ribs that fall right off the bone, with a sweet, smoky barbecue sauce. Low heat and time.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 1000 g pork ribs (spare ribs)
  • 2 tbsp brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp paprika (smoked, if you have it)
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 250 ml store-bought barbecue sauce (or homemade)
  • salt and pepper

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Remove the thin membrane from the back of the ribs (pull it off with a paper towel — it comes off in one piece). It's what makes them tough.
  2. Mix the sugar, paprika, garlic and onion powders, salt, and pepper. Rub it well all over the meat.
  3. Wrap tightly in aluminum foil, meat side down.
  4. Low oven, 150°C, for 2½ hours. Low and slow — there are no shortcuts.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Unwrap and brush generously with barbecue sauce.
  6. Back in the oven (or on the grill) at 200°C for 15 minutes, brushing once more, until the sauce is shiny and sticky. Rest 10 minutes and cut between the bones.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

ColeslawBoiled or grilled cornFrench fries or roasted potatoesCornbread, for the full menu
Lili's tipThe test is simple: the meat should give way and almost fall off the bone when you lift a rib with tongs. If it resists, it needs more time, not more heat.

American Apple Pie

Tarte de maçã americana
Prep30 min
Cooking50 min
Total80 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

The pie from the movies: cinnamon apples inside a golden, flaky crust.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 2 sheets shortcrust or puff pastry (store-bought works fine)
  • 6 apples, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 120 g sugar
  • 1 tbsp flour
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 20 g butter, cut into small cubes
  • 1 beaten egg with a little milk, for brushing; a pinch of salt and nutmeg

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the apples with the sugar, flour, cinnamon, lemon, salt, and nutmeg. Let it sit 15 minutes — they release juice and soak up the flavor.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  2. Line a pie dish with one sheet of pastry, leaving extra around the edges.
  3. Put the apples in, with the little butter cubes on top.
  4. Cover with the second sheet: either whole (with a few slits on top to let the steam out), or in crisscross strips, like in the classic photos.
  5. Trim and fold the edges, and brush with the beaten egg.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  6. Bake at 190°C for 45 to 50 minutes, until golden and the filling is bubbling. Let it cool for at least 1 hour before slicing, so the filling sets.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A scoop of vanilla ice cream (à la mode, as they say there)Whipped creamA slice of cheddar cheese on top — an old tradition in parts of the US, try it before you judge!
Lili's tipThe cooling hour isn't wasted time: a pie sliced while hot falls apart and the filling runs everywhere.

Chocolate Cake with Creamy Frosting

Bolo de chocolate com cobertura cremosa
Prep20 min
Cooking35 min
Total55 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves8 people

The fluffy chocolate cake with the creamy frosting from the techniques page. The birthday favorite.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 250 g flour
  • 75 g cocoa powder
  • 300 g sugar
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 3 eggs
  • 200 ml milk
  • 120 ml oil
  • 200 ml hot water
  • 200 g butter at room temperature (frosting)
  • 300 g powdered sugar (frosting)
  • 50 g cocoa (frosting) and 3 to 4 tbsp of milk

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Oven at 180°C. Grease and flour a 22 cm round pan (or two 20 cm pans).💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Mix the dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, and a pinch of salt.
  3. Add the eggs, milk, and oil and beat for 2 minutes. Pour in the hot water a little at a time — the batter will be runny, that's how it should be (it's what makes the cake moist).
  4. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes. The toothpick should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
  5. Let it cool completely before frosting — frosting on a warm cake melts and slides off.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  6. Creamy frosting: beat the butter for 2 minutes, add the sifted powdered sugar and cocoa and the milk, and beat until light and spreadable. Spread it between the layers and on top, with swirls of the spatula.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A glass of really cold milkCoffee, for the adultsVanilla ice cream on the side
Lili's tipChocolate cake keeps, covered, at room temperature for 2 days — in the fridge it dries out. Take it out 30 minutes before serving.

Brazilian Carrot Cake with Brigadeiro Frosting

Bolo de cenoura com cobertura de brigadeiro
Prep15 min
Cooking40 min
Total55 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves8 people

Brazil's orange cake: carrots blended into the batter and a generous layer of soft brigadeiro on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 3 medium carrots, peeled
  • 4 eggs
  • 240 ml oil
  • 300 g sugar
  • 320 g flour
  • 1 tbsp baking powder
  • 1 can sweetened condensed milk (frosting)
  • 3 tbsp cocoa (frosting) and 1 tbsp of butter

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Blend the carrots, eggs, oil, and sugar in the blender until you get a smooth orange cream.
  2. Pour it into a bowl, add the sifted flour, and stir. The baking powder goes in last — just fold it in.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.
  3. Greased 24 cm pan, oven at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  4. Frosting: put the condensed milk, cocoa, and butter in a pan over the heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens a little (soft brigadeiro stage, about 6 minutes).
  5. Pour the warm frosting over the warm cake — it should drip down the sides, just like that.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Freshly brewed coffeeA glass of milkOn its own, as a snack — like in Brazil

Pineapple Upside-Down Cake

Bolo de ananás virado
Prep20 min
Cooking40 min
Total60 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves8 people

It bakes upside down: the caramelized pineapple sits at the bottom of the pan and becomes the star when you unmold it.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 1 can pineapple rings (save the juice)
  • 100 g brown sugar
  • 50 g butter
  • 200 g flour
  • 180 g sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 100 ml milk or pineapple juice
  • 1 tsp baking powder; cherries in syrup (if you like, for the center of the rings)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Melt the butter in the bottom of a 24 cm pan, spread the brown sugar over it, and arrange the pineapple rings nicely on top — this is the side that will show.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Beat the eggs and sugar, add the milk, flour, and baking powder, without overbeating.
  3. Pour the batter over the pineapple, carefully so you don't move it.💡 Why it matters: Not stirring is a technique too: it gives crusts time to form, rice time to absorb, and fish time to stay in one piece.
  4. Oven at 180°C for 35 to 40 minutes.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  5. Rest for 10 minutes and flip the cake onto the serving plate with one confident move. If a ring stays in the pan, take it out and put it back in place — nobody notices.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Whipped creamVanilla or coconut ice creamTea, as a snack
Lili's tipUnmold it warm, never cold: cold caramel sticks the pineapple to the pan.

Banana Bread Cake

Bolo de banana
Prep10 min
Cooking50 min
Total60 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves8 people

The fix for very ripe bananas: a moist, dense cake that smells of cinnamon.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 3 very ripe bananas
  • 2 eggs
  • 150 g brown sugar
  • 80 g melted butter
  • 250 g flour
  • 1 tsp baking powder and another of cinnamon
  • chopped walnuts (if you like); a pinch of salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mash the bananas with a fork — leave a few chunks.
  2. Mix the eggs, sugar, and butter. Add the banana.
  3. Fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Add the walnuts if using.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Pour into a loaf pan lined with parchment paper.
  5. Oven at 175°C for 45 to 50 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes before slicing.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Peanut butter spread on the sliceGreek yogurtCoffee or tea, at breakfast
Lili's tipThe riper (and more spotted) the banana, the sweeter and better the cake. Green bananas don't work here.

Chocolate Chip Cookies

Cookies de chocolate
Prep15 min
Cooking12 min
Total27 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

American cookies: crispy edges, a soft center, and melting chocolate chips.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 120 g melted butter
  • 150 g brown sugar and 50 g of white sugar
  • 1 egg and 1 tsp of vanilla
  • 220 g flour
  • 0,5 tsp baking soda
  • 150 g chocolate chips

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the butter and sugars. Add the egg and vanilla.
  2. Add the flour, baking soda, and a pinch of salt, just until it comes together. Fold in the chips.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  3. Chill the dough for 30 minutes in the fridge — it makes all the difference to the texture.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  4. Make walnut-sized balls, well spaced, on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  5. Oven at 180°C for 10 to 12 minutes: golden edges and the center still soft. They cool (and firm up) on the sheet.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A glass of cold milk — the classic pairingIce cream, between two cookies (an ice cream sandwich)Coffee
Lili's tipTake them out of the oven looking 'still raw' in the middle. That's exactly right: they finish cooking with the heat of the sheet.

Butter Cookies

Bolachas de manteiga
Prep15 min
Cooking15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

The simple cookies of always: butter, a touch of lemon, and tea on the side.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 200 g butter at room temperature
  • 120 g sugar
  • 1 egg
  • 300 g flour
  • 1 lemon (just the zest)
  • a pinch of salt; sugar for sprinkling

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Beat the butter and sugar until creamy.
  2. Add the egg and the lemon zest.
  3. Fold in the flour and salt until it becomes a dough. Don't knead too much.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Roll it out (0.5 cm) and cut with cookie cutters or a glass.
  5. Baking sheet with parchment paper, oven at 180°C for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  6. Cool on a rack — warm, they seem soft; cold, they turn crisp.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Tea or coffeeMilk, for the kidsIn a pretty tin, they make a homemade gift
Lili's tipDough too soft? 20 minutes in the fridge and it rolls out without sticking.

Chocolate Brownies

Brownie de chocolate
Prep15 min
Cooking25 min
Total40 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves8 people

Dense, moist, and with that thin, shiny crust on top. It's not cake — it's a brownie.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 170 g butter
  • 200 g dark chocolate
  • 3 eggs
  • 200 g sugar
  • 90 g flour
  • 30 g cocoa
  • a pinch of salt; walnuts (if you like)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Melt the butter and chocolate together (microwave in short bursts, or a double boiler). Let it cool a little.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Beat the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes, until slightly thickened — that's what makes the shiny crust.
  3. Add the melted chocolate and stir.
  4. Fold in the flour, cocoa, and salt, just until the flour disappears.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Lined 20 cm square pan, oven at 175°C for 22 to 25 minutes. The center should wobble slightly.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  6. Cool completely before cutting into squares — warm, it falls apart.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Vanilla ice cream (warm brownie + ice cream = a classic)CoffeeA drizzle of caramel on top
Lili's tipMistake #1 is overbaking. A dry brownie is just a sad cake: take it out while the center is still moist.

No-Bake Berry Cheesecake

Cheesecake de frutos vermelhos

Cooking0 min
Total25 min

Serves8 people

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 200 g crushed digestive cookies
  • 80 g melted butter
  • 400 g cream cheese
  • 200 ml heavy cream, for whipping
  • 100 g powdered sugar and the juice of half a lemon
  • 200 g berries (fresh or frozen)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the cookie crumbs with the butter and press firmly into the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan. Put it in the fridge.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  2. Beat the cream cheese with the sugar and lemon until smooth.
  3. Whip the cream until firm and fold it into the cheese, gently.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Pour the cream over the base, smooth it out, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight is better).
  5. Before serving, cover with the berries (if frozen, thaw and drain them).💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

🍽️ What to serve it with

A coffee, after a light dinnerExtra berry coulisLittle mint leaves on top, for the photo
Lili's tipA springform pan is half the battle: without one, the first slice always comes out broken.

Chicken Tikka Masala

Frango tikka masala
Prep20 min
Cooking30 min
Total50 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

The world's most famous Indian curry: chicken marinated in yogurt, in a creamy tomato and spice sauce.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g chicken, cut into cubes
  • 150 g plain yogurt (marinade) and 2 cloves of garlic + grated ginger
  • 2 tsp garam masala
  • 400 g crushed tomatoes
  • 1 finely chopped onion
  • 150 ml heavy cream
  • oil, salt, paprika, and cilantro

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with garlic, ginger, salt, and half the garam masala, for at least 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Sear the chicken in a very hot skillet until it takes on color. Set aside (it doesn't need to be cooked through).💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In the same skillet, sauté the onion until well golden. Add the tomato and the rest of the spices and cook for 10 minutes, until the sauce darkens and thickens.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Blend the sauce (optional, for a velvety texture) and return it to the skillet with the cream.
  5. Add the chicken and cook for 8 to 10 minutes in the sauce.
  6. Serve with cilantro on top.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Basmati rice or jeera riceGarlic naanRaita (yogurt with cucumber) on the side
Lili's tipA blended, well-reduced sauce is the difference between 'homemade curry' and 'restaurant curry'.

Chicken Biryani

Biryani de frango
Prep30 min
Cooking45 min
Total75 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

India's celebration rice: fragrant basmati layered with spiced chicken and fried onion.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 300 g basmati rice, soaked 30 min
  • 500 g chicken, in pieces
  • 150 g yogurt
  • 2 onions, thinly sliced (half fried until golden)
  • 2 tsp biryani mix or garam masala + saffron in warm milk
  • garlic, ginger, bay leaves, cardamom, salt, oil, and cilantro/mint

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with garlic, ginger, spices, and salt, for 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Cook the rice in well-salted water with bay leaf and cardamom only to 70% — still firm in the middle. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  3. Cook the marinated chicken in its pot for 15 minutes, until it forms a thick sauce.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  4. Layer it in the pot: rice, chicken, fried onion, herbs, a drizzle of the saffron milk. Repeat.
  5. Cover tightly (the lid wrapped in a cloth, the way it's done there) and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, without opening.
  6. Rest for 10 minutes and fold it gently, from the bottom up, right at the table.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Yogurt and cucumber raitaOnion and tomato saladNaan
Lili's tipThe rice at 70% is the critical point: it finishes cooking in the chicken's steam. Fully cooked beforehand, it turns to mush.

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 2 boiled potatoes, cut into small cubes
  • 100 g peas
  • 1 chopped onion, garlic, ginger, and 1 tsp of garam masala + cumin

  5. Drain on paper and serve hot.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 250 g red lentils, well rinsed
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 2 cloves garlic and grated ginger
  • 1 tsp turmeric and another of cumin
  • 400 ml water or broth (more, if needed)
  • oil or ghee, salt, lemon, and cilantro

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sauté the onion in oil until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and spices, 1 minute.
  2. Add the lentils and the water. Cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then — they fall apart on their own.
  3. If it gets too thick, add hot water: dahl should be like a thick soup.
  4. Season with salt and a few drops of lemon.
  5. Final trick (tadka): heat a drizzle of oil with cumin and sliced garlic until it sizzles and pour it over the top, already in the bowl.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Jeera riceNaanSautéed spinach on the side
Lili's tipRed lentils don't need soaking and cook fast — it's the easiest Indian recipe to start with.

Brazilian Beef Escondidinho with Cassava Mash

Escondidinho de carne com puré de mandioca
Prep25 min
Cooking35 min
Total60 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Seasoned beef 'hidden' under a creamy cassava mash, baked until golden on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 800 g cassava (yuca), peeled and cut into chunks
  • 400 g ground beef or shredded dried beef, already soaked
  • 1 chopped onion and 2 cloves of garlic
  • 2 chopped tomatoes
  • 100 ml milk and 1 tbsp of butter (for the mash)
  • 100 g shredded cheese
  • olive oil, salt, pepper, and parsley

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil the cassava in salted water until very soft, about 25 minutes. Remove the fibrous core.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Make a mash with the hot milk and butter. Season it — it should be creamy, not dry.
  3. Sauté the onion and garlic, add the beef, and brown it. Add the tomato and cook for 8 minutes, until it's a moist filling but without too much sauce.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. In a baking dish: beef on the bottom, mash on top, smoothed with a wet spoon.
  5. Cheese on top and oven at 200°C for 15 minutes, until golden and bubbling.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green saladWhite rice on the sideTomato and onion vinaigrette
Lili's tipDry cassava mash cracks in the oven. If it's too firm, add more hot milk without fear.

Brazilian Chicken Stroganoff

Prep10 min
Cooking20 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

The Brazilian version of stroganoff: creamy, with ketchup and mustard, and potato sticks on top — always.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g chicken, cut into cubes
  • 1 chopped onion and 2 cloves of garlic
  • 200 g mushrooms (optional, but classic)
  • 3 tbsp ketchup and 1 tbsp of mustard
  • 200 ml heavy cream
  • olive oil, salt, pepper; potato sticks, to serve

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the chicken and brown it in very hot olive oil, in two batches so it sears instead of steaming. Set aside.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  2. Sauté the onion, garlic, and mushrooms in the same skillet.
  3. Return the chicken, add the ketchup and mustard, and stir for 1 minute.
  4. Lower the heat, add the cream, and warm it without boiling, 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce is pink and creamy.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Serve right away, with the potato sticks on top at the table — never inside the pot.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White rice (mandatory)Potato sticks (also mandatory)A simple salad
Lili's tipBoiling cream curdles and separates. Finished sauce = low heat and no rushing at the end.

Beans with cassava flour, collard greens, and bacon — the food of the travelers of Minas Gerais.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 400 g cooked and drained beans (black-eyed peas or carioca beans)
  • 150 g bacon, cut into cubes
  • 100 g sausage (linguiça), sliced into rounds
  • 150 g cassava flour
  • 200 g collard greens, cut very thin
  • 3 hard-boiled or scrambled eggs, in pieces

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Fry the bacon and sausage until golden. Keep the fat in the skillet — it's flavor.
  2. Sauté the onion and garlic in that fat.
  3. Add the drained beans and stir for 3 minutes, without broth.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  4. Add the flour a little at a time, stirring, until it's loose like a moist farofa.
  5. Add the collards only at the end, 1 minute — they should stay bright green.
  6. Mix in the eggs and serve right away.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White riceOrange slicesPork ribs or roast chicken on the sidePiri-piri for those who like it
Lili's tipToo much flour dries the dish out. Add it little by little and stop when it's loose, not when the package is empty.

Brazilian Tapioca Crepe

Tapioca com queijo
Prep5 min
Cooking5 min
Total10 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves2 people

A gluten-free crepe made with just tapioca starch, in a skillet, in three minutes.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 100 g hydrated tapioca starch (sold ready to use)
  • 4 slices cheese (mozzarella or queijo coalho)
  • a pinch of salt; butter (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Sift the starch straight into a cold nonstick skillet, spreading it in a thin, even layer.💡 Why it matters: Sifting removes lumps and adds air to dry ingredients — lighter batters and sauces without little balls.
  2. Turn the heat to medium. In 1 to 2 minutes the starch binds and becomes a disc — you don't flip it.
  3. Put the cheese on one half, fold it in half, and wait for it to melt, 1 minute.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Serve right away, still warm and flexible.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Coffee, like in Brazil's NortheastFillings: cream cheese (requeijão), coconut with condensed milk (sweet), shredded chicken, scrambled eggFruit juice on the side
Lili's tipA thin, even layer is everything. Too thick, it turns rubbery; with holes, it breaks when you fold it.

Cooking35 min

Cod loins roasted in plenty of good olive oil, with smashed baby potatoes and golden garlic.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 4 loins desalted cod
  • 600 g baby potatoes, skin on
  • 6 cloves sliced garlic
  • 200 ml good olive oil (it is the sauce!)
  • bay leaves, salt, pepper, and parsley; olives (if you like)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil the baby potatoes in their skins in salted water until almost tender. Give each one a gentle smash so it cracks open.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Put the cod in a baking tray, the smashed potatoes around it, the bay leaves, and half the olive oil.
  3. Oven at 200°C for 20 minutes.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  4. Heat the rest of the olive oil with the sliced garlic until lightly golden — careful, burnt garlic is bitter.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  5. Pour the very hot garlic oil over everything, right at the table. Sprinkle with parsley.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Sautéed turnip greens or spinachTomato saladBread for the olive oil — you'll need it
Lili's tip'Lagareiro' comes from lagar, the olive oil mill. Here the olive oil isn't a seasoning: it's a main ingredient. Use the best you have.

Portuguese Steak, Egg & Fries — Bitoque

Bitoque
Prep10 min
Cooking20 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves2 people

Portugal's most beloved tavern dish: steak with garlic and bay leaf, a fried egg on top, and french fries.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 2 thin beef steaks
  • 3 cloves crushed garlic
  • 2 leaves bay leaves
  • 50 ml white wine
  • 2 eggs
  • 300 g potatoes, for frying
  • butter and olive oil, salt and pepper; rice and salad, to serve

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the steaks with garlic, bay leaf, salt, and pepper. Let them sit for 15 minutes.
  2. Fry the potatoes until golden and salt them. Keep them warm.
  3. Really hot skillet with olive oil and a little butter: fry the steaks 2 to 3 minutes per side.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Remove the steaks, pour the wine into the skillet, and scrape the bottom — that's the sauce, 1 minute.
  5. Fry the eggs and put one on top of each steak ('a cavalo' — riding on top).
  6. Serve with the sauce over it all, fries, rice, and salad on the same plate, like at the tavern.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White rice and salad (the classic trio)Bread for the sauceA glass of the house red wine, for the adults
Lili's tipA thin steak cooks fast. A properly hot skillet and little time — a gray, dry bitoque is the only real mistake possible.

Alentejo Bread & Coriander Soup

Açorda alentejana
Prep10 min
Cooking15 min
Total25 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

A soup of bread, garlic, and cilantro with a poached egg — humble in origin, incredibly rich in flavor.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 200 g Alentejo or rustic bread, preferably a day old, sliced
  • 4 cloves garlic
  • 1 large bunch cilantro
  • 4 eggs
  • 1200 ml boiling water
  • a generous amount of olive oil, and salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Pound the garlic with the cilantro and salt in a mortar (or chop everything very finely) until it becomes a green paste.
  2. Put the paste in a serving bowl, add a good drizzle of olive oil, and lay the bread slices on top.
  3. Poach the eggs in the boiling salted water, 3 minutes, and lift them out with a slotted spoon.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Pour the boiling water over the bread, cover, and wait 5 minutes — the bread swells and becomes a thick soup.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Uncover, stir once, and put a poached egg on each plate.

🍽️ What to serve it with

On its own, as a complete light mealWith shredded boiled cod on top (the rich version)Alentejo olives on the side
Lili's tipAçorda doesn't go back on the heat once the water goes in. If you cook it, it loses its soul — it's a bowl soup, not a pot soup.
