Prawn Rissoles

Rissóis de camarão
Prep40 min
Cooking20 min
Total60 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves6 people

Thin pastry half-moons with a shrimp cream filling — a party snack in Mozambique and Portugal.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 250 g flour (dough) and 250 ml of water + 1 tbsp of butter
  • 300 g peeled shrimp, chopped
  • 200 ml milk and 1 tbsp of flour (for the cream)
  • 1 finely chopped onion and 1 clove of garlic
  • parsley, salt, pepper, lemon; egg and breadcrumbs, for coating; oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Dough: boil the water with butter and salt, add the flour all at once, and stir until it forms a smooth ball. Knead it while warm and let it rest, covered.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  2. Filling: sauté the onion and garlic, add the shrimp for 2 minutes. Sprinkle the flour, add the milk a little at a time until it becomes a thick cream. Season with salt, pepper, lemon, and parsley. Let it cool completely.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  3. Roll the dough out thin and cut circles of 9-10 cm.
  4. Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold into a half-moon, and seal the edges with a fork.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Dip in egg and breadcrumbs and fry in hot oil until golden.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Mild piri-piri sauceA simple saladAs a party appetizer, with cold juices
Lili's tipThe rissóis dough is the same as coxinha dough — cooked in the pot. And a cold, thick filling is what keeps them from bursting in the oil.

Chakalaka: spicy beans and vegetables. Pap: a firm white cornmeal porridge, a cousin of xima.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 1 can cooked beans (400 g)
  • 1 onion, 1 bell pepper and 2 grated carrots
  • 2 chopped tomatoes

  • 250 g white cornmeal (for the pap)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Chakalaka: sauté the onion, bell pepper and carrot in oil for 5 minutes. Add the curry powder and the tomato and cook for 10 minutes.
  2. Add the beans with a little of their liquid and cook for 10 more minutes. It should be thick and spicy. Adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  3. Pap: boil the water with salt. Pour the cornmeal in a thin stream, stirring constantly with a strong wooden spoon.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Cook the pap over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring hard now and then, until it is firm and pulls away from the pot.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Serve the pap in small mounds with the chakalaka on top or on the side.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Grilled meat (braai!) — the classic pairingRoast chickenGreen salad
Lili's tipPap and xima are from the same family: the difference is the texture. South African pap is made firmer, so it can hold the sauce on top.

Malva Pudding

Pudim Malva
Prep15 min
Cooking35 min
Total50 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

An apricot sponge cake soaked in a hot butter-and-cream sauce while still warm. Pure comfort.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 200 g sugar and 2 eggs
  • 200 g flour and 1 tsp baking soda
  • 2 tbsp apricot jam
  • 200 ml milk and 1 tbsp vinegar
  • 150 ml heavy cream + 50 g butter + 80 g sugar (sauce)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Beat the eggs and sugar until fluffy. Add the apricot jam.
  2. Fold in the flour and baking soda, alternating with the milk mixed with vinegar.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  3. Greased baking dish, oven at 180°C for 30 to 35 minutes, until well golden.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  4. Sauce: boil the cream, butter and sugar for 2 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, poke it with a fork and slowly pour the hot sauce over it — it drinks it all up.
  6. Serve warm.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Whipped cream or vanilla ice creamCustard — the classic South African pairingCoffee, after a braai
Lili's tipPour the sauce over the piping-hot cake in two goes: half, wait for it to soak in, then the other half. That is what makes it moist inside.

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Season the chicken and grill or boil it until tender. Shred it with two forks.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Warm the shredded chicken in a skillet with a little of the cooking water and adjust the seasonings — it should be juicy, not dry.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.

  5. Everyone builds their own taco: tortilla, chicken, fresh toppings, a squeeze of lime.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Guacamole and nachosMexican-style rice (with tomato and peas)Seasoned black beans on the side
Lili's tipA cold tortilla cracks; a warm tortilla folds. The 30 seconds in the dry skillet are not optional.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 2 very ripe avocados
  • 0,5 red onion, finely chopped
  • 1 tomato, seeded and finely diced
  • 1 lime (the juice)
  • chopped cilantro, salt and piri-piri or jalapeño (if you like); nachos, to serve

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cut the avocados open, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
  2. Mash with a fork — chunky, never in a blender.
  3. Add the onion, tomato, cilantro, salt and the lime juice right away, so it doesn't turn brown.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Taste and adjust: guacamole without salt and lime tastes like nothing, no matter how good the fruit is.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  5. Serve right away, with the nachos around it.

🍽️ What to serve it with

As a starter for a Mexican dinnerOn top of tacos and quesadillasWith scrambled eggs, for a Mexican breakfast
Lili's tipA ripe avocado gives under the palm of your hand without you squeezing with your fingers. Hard = flavorless and impossible to mash well.

Serves 2 people

  • 120 g grated cheese that melts well

  1. Season the chicken with cumin, paprika and salt.
  2. Spread cheese over half of each tortilla, chicken and bell pepper on top, then a little more cheese (it is the 'glue').
  3. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  4. Rest 1 minute and cut into triangles.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

GuacamoleSour cream or yogurtA simple salad with lime
Lili's tipCheese on both sides of the filling glues the quesadilla shut. Only in the middle, and it all falls open when you cut it.

Churros with Chocolate Sauce

Churros com chocolate
Prep20 min
Cooking15 min
Total35 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Fried dough sticks rolled in cinnamon sugar, for dipping in thick, hot chocolate.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 250 ml water and 50 g butter
  • 150 g flour
  • 2 eggs
  • 100 g sugar with 1 tsp cinnamon (for coating)
  • 150 g dark chocolate + 150 ml milk and 1 tsp cornstarch (sauce)
  • oil for frying; a pinch of salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil the water with the butter and salt. Add the flour all at once and stir until it forms a smooth ball (it is the same dough as the rissoles!).💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Take it off the heat, let it cool a little and add the eggs one at a time, beating well — you get a thick, shiny dough.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  3. Put the dough in a piping bag fitted with a large star tip.
  4. Pipe 12–15 cm strips straight into the hot oil, cutting them with scissors. Fry until golden.
  5. Drain and roll them immediately in the cinnamon sugar, while still hot.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  6. Sauce: heat the milk with the chocolate and cornstarch until thickened. Serve the churros with the chocolate on the side, for dipping.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Coffee or milk, as a snackAs the end of a Mexican dinnerOn their own, still warm — the best way
Lili's tipNo piping bag? Use a freezer bag with one corner cut off. The ridges from the star tip are what give the classic crunch, but the flavor is the same.

Easy Chicken Ramen

Ramen fácil de frango
Prep15 min
Cooking25 min
Total40 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves2 people

The Japanese noodle soup: rich broth, chicken, an egg with a creamy yolk, and everything arranged nicely on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 1200 ml chicken broth
  • 2 breasts chicken
  • 2 eggs
  • 150 g ramen noodles or egg noodles
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp miso paste (if you have it)
  • ginger, garlic, scallions, corn and sesame oil

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil the eggs for 6 and a half minutes in boiling water. Run them under cold water and peel — the yolk should stay creamy.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Cook the chicken in the broth with ginger and garlic for 12 minutes. Take it out and shred or slice it.
  3. Season the broth with soy sauce and miso. Taste it: it should be full of flavor, it is what seasons everything.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  4. Cook the noodles separately, for the time on the package. Drain.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  5. Build the bowls: noodles, hot broth over them, chicken, half an egg, corn and scallions. A drizzle of sesame oil at the end.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Gyoza or onigiri on the sideGreen teaOn its own — a bowl of ramen is a meal
Lili's tipThe 6-and-a-half-minute egg is sacred in ramen: a hard yolk ruins the bowl, a runny yolk gets lost in the broth.

Onigiri — Japanese Rice Balls

Onigiri
Prep20 min
Cooking15 min
Total35 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Triangular rice balls with a filling, wrapped in seaweed. Japan's go-to snack.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 300 g sushi rice or short-grain rice
  • 4 sheets nori seaweed, cut in half
  • 100 g filling: tuna with mayo, shredded salmon or umeboshi plum
  • salt and water (for wetting your hands)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the rice with water only (no seasonings) and let it cool a little, covered.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Wet your hands in salted water — without this, the rice sticks all to you instead of to the little ball.
  3. Put a handful of rice in your palm, make a little dent, and add a spoonful of filling.
  4. Cover with a little more rice and press it into a triangle shape, turning it between your hands, firmly but without squashing it.
  5. Wrap the base with the strip of nori, like a handle.
  6. Eat it within the next few hours — onigiri doesn't like the fridge (the rice hardens).💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Miso soupGreen teaIn a lunch box, like in Japan
Lili's tipRice that is too hot burns your hands, and cold rice won't shape. Lukewarm is the right point — you work it at body temperature, like with sandwiches.

The Japanese cabbage 'pizza-pancake': crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, with sauces on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 150 g flour and 150 ml water or broth
  • 2 eggs
  • 250 g cabbage, sliced very thin
  • 2 scallions, sliced
  • salt, oil; to serve: Japanese mayo, okonomiyaki sauce or mild barbecue sauce, bonito flakes and seaweed (if you have them)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the flour, water and eggs until you have a thick batter. Season with salt.
  2. Add the cabbage and scallions and fold them in — it looks like too much cabbage, but that's how it is (it wilts in the skillet).💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  3. Heat oil in a skillet, pour in all the batter and flatten it into a disc about 2 cm thick.
  4. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, until the base is golden and firm.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Flip it with the help of a plate (be brave!) and cook 4 to 5 more minutes.
  6. Put it on a plate and draw the sauces on top in a zigzag — the classic presentation.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Miso soupCucumber saladAs a quick one-dish dinner
Lili's tipThe name means 'grilled as you like it': add whatever you have — bacon, shrimp, cheese, corn. The cabbage base can handle it all.

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 300 g strong flour (or all-purpose)
  • 1 tsp instant dry yeast and another tsp of salt
  • 200 ml warm water
  • 200 g crushed tomatoes with salt and oregano (sauce)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the flour, yeast and salt. Add the warm water and knead for 8 to 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. (Photo 1: kneading)

  3. Turn the oven to its maximum (250°C) with the baking tray inside heating up.
  4. Stretch the dough on a floured surface, from the center outward, leaving a higher edge. (Photo 3: stretching it out and adding the sauce)
  5. A thin layer of sauce (too much sauce makes it soggy), mozzarella and toppings.
  6. Bake it on the hot tray for 8 to 12 minutes, until the edge is golden and bubbling. Basil at the end.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green salad with lemonAs a movie night at homeWith the bruschetta from the Italian page, as a starter
Lili's tipA home oven never reaches the 450°C of pizza ovens — make up for it with the preheated tray, which imitates the hot stone.

Potato Gnocchi with Tomato Sauce

Gnocchi de batata com molho de tomate
Prep30 min
Cooking15 min
Total45 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Little potato pillows that float when they're ready. Easier than they look.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g floury potatoes, cooked and well drained
  • 180 g flour (plus a little more for the counter)
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 400 g crushed tomatoes, garlic and basil (sauce)
  • salt, olive oil and Parmesan

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mash the potatoes while still warm until you have a very smooth, dry purée. Let it cool a little.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Add the yolk, salt and the flour a little at a time, kneading only until it comes together — overworked dough turns tough.
  3. Roll ropes as thick as a finger, cut 2 cm pieces and mark each one with the tines of a fork.
  4. Cook in boiling salted water, in two batches: when they float, they're ready (1 to 2 minutes).💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  5. Meanwhile, heat the tomato sauce with garlic and olive oil. Put the gnocchi straight into the sauce, with a little of the cooking water.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  6. Serve with Parmesan and basil.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green saladAs a light main dishWith a butter and sage sauce, in the classic variation
Lili's tipThe trick is dry potatoes: potatoes boiled in their skins (or baked) hold less water and need less flour — and less flour = light gnocchi.

🧺 Ingredients

  • 60 g sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla
  • 2 leaves gelatin (or 1 tsp powdered gelatin)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

Crispy oven-baked wings tossed in a spicy butter sauce. For eating with your hands and plenty of napkins.

  1. Dry the wings very well with paper towels. Mix with the salt, garlic powder and baking powder.
  2. Place them on a rack over a baking tray and bake at 220°C for 30 to 35 minutes, turning halfway, until very crispy.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Mix the hot sauce with the melted butter.
  4. Put the wings in a large bowl, pour the sauce over and toss to coat them all.
  5. Serve right away, with the vegetable sticks and the white dip on the side.

🍽️ What to serve it with

French friesColeslawBeer or very cold lemonade
Lili's tipThe baking powder on the skin changes the pH and gives you fried-level crispiness in the oven. It's not a recipe mistake — it's science, and it works.

Cod with Cream

Bacalhau com natas

Cooking30 min
Total50 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

The Sunday classic: shredded cod, matchstick potatoes and a creamy gratinéed sauce.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 g desalted cod, cooked and shredded
  • 400 g matchstick potato chips or potatoes fried in thin sticks
  • 1 onion in half-moons and 2 garlic cloves
  • 400 ml milk
  • 200 ml heavy cream
  • 2 tbsp flour and 2 tbsp butter (for the sauce)
  • olive oil, salt, pepper, nutmeg and grated cheese (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the cod for 8 minutes, save the cooking water and shred it, removing the bones and skin.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft and sweet, without browning too much.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. Add the cod and toss for 2 minutes. Season with pepper.
  4. Make the sauce: melt the butter, add the flour and stir for 1 minute; pour in the milk a little at a time, stirring constantly, until thickened. Add the cream and nutmeg.
  5. Mix the cod, the matchstick potatoes and half the sauce. Transfer to a baking dish, cover with the rest of the sauce and cheese if you use it.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Oven at 200°C for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top. Rest 5 minutes before serving.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green salad with onionBlack olivesWhite rice, if you want to stretch the meal
Lili's tipThe cod is already salty: taste before adding salt to the sauce. It's easier to fix at the end than to save an over-salted dish.

Portuguese Leite-Creme — Custard with Caramelised Sugar

Leite-creme
Prep10 min
Cooking15 min
Total25 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

A smooth milk-and-lemon custard with a burnt-sugar crust on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 ml milk
  • 4 egg yolks
  • 100 g sugar
  • 1 tbsp cornstarch
  • 1 peel of lemon and 1 cinnamon stick
  • sugar for burning on top; ground cinnamon (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Heat the milk with the lemon peel and cinnamon until almost boiling. Take it off the heat and let the flavors infuse for 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Beat the yolks, sugar and cornstarch until pale.
  3. Pour the hot milk in a thin stream over the yolks, stirring constantly, so they don't cook all of a sudden.
  4. Return everything to low heat and stir until it thickens like a custard. Don't let it boil.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  5. Pour into bowls, let it cool and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  6. Before serving, sprinkle with sugar and burn it with a kitchen torch or a hot iron until it forms a crust.

🍽️ What to serve it with

On its own, well chilledWith butter cookiesAfter a cod dish — the classic ending
Lili's tipThe custard keeps thickening off the heat too. Take it off when it still looks a little loose: cold, it will be just right.

Serves 4 people

Brazilian Prawn Bobó — Cassava & Coconut Stew

Bobó de camarão

Cooking25 min
Total50 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Prawns in a cassava, coconut milk and tomato cream — Brazilian comfort food from Bahia.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 500 g cassava (yuca), peeled
  • 500 g peeled prawns
  • 1 onion, 1 bell pepper and 2 chopped tomatoes
  • 400 ml coconut milk
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • olive oil (and dendê palm oil, if you have it), salt, lemon, cilantro and piri-piri

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the cassava in salted water until very soft. Save some of the water.
  2. Blend the cassava with a little of the cooking water and half the coconut milk until you have a thick cream.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  3. Sauté the onion, bell pepper, garlic and tomato in olive oil until they form a sauce.
  4. Add the cassava cream and the rest of the coconut milk. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring — it sticks to the bottom easily.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  5. Season and sear the prawns separately for 2 minutes, and add them to the cream only at the end, with lemon and cilantro.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  6. If you have dendê, a drizzle at the end gives color and the Bahian flavor. Serve hot.

🍽️ What to serve it with

White rice (a must)Simple farofaTomato vinaigrette
Lili's tipThe prawns go in at the end because the cream is already hot: they only need 3 to 4 minutes so they don't toughen.

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 200 g frozen unsweetened açaí pulp
  • 1 frozen banana
  • 50 ml milk or plant-based drink, only as much as needed

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Break the açaí pulp into pieces and put it in the blender with the frozen banana.

  4. Pour into chilled bowls.💡 Why it matters: Cold firms up creams and doughs and makes everything easier to cut and handle — and it's also a safety thing with cream and eggs.
  5. Top with granola, banana and strawberries only when it's time to eat.

🍽️ What to serve it with

For a hearty breakfastAfter a workout (add protein powder, if you like)With powdered milk on top, like they do in Brazil
Lili's tipThe granola really goes on at the end: on top of the frozen açaí it stays crunchy; mixed in early, it goes soft.

Serves 2 people

  • 4 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  • 60 ml good olive oil
  • 0,5 tsp chili flakes
  • chopped parsley, salt and Parmesan (optional — in Rome, often without cheese)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the pasta in well-salted water. Save a cup of the cooking water before draining.💡 Why it matters: Cooking water holds starch and salt: it helps sauces bind, shine and cling to the food instead of staying watery on the plate.
  2. Meanwhile, warm the olive oil over low heat with the garlic and chili.   4. Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss for 1 minute, adding more water if it dries out.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

  • 50 g flour, for coating the chicken

Crispy Fried Chicken

Frango frito crocante
Prep25 min
Cooking25 min
Total50 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

Chicken marinated in buttermilk, well breaded and fried until golden and crackly.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 800 g chicken pieces, bone-in and skin-on
  • 300 ml buttermilk, or milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 250 g flour
  • 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and another tsp of onion powder
  • salt, pepper and oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Marinate the chicken in the buttermilk with salt for at least 2 hours (overnight is better). The acid tenderizes the meat.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Mix the flour with the spices and salt. Add 2 spoonfuls of the marinade to the flour and rub it in — the lumps become extra crust.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  3. Coat the chicken in the flour, pressing well so it sticks. Rest 10 minutes: the crust holds on better.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Heat oil over medium heat (about 170°C) in a deep pot.
  5. Fry for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until well golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack, not on paper — paper softens the crust.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  6. Salt on top as soon as it comes out of the oil. Rest 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

ColeslawFrench fries or mashed potatoesButtered corn on the cobHoney mustard sauce
Lili's tipDon't crowd the pot: too many pieces drop the oil temperature and the crust turns soft and greasy.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 250 g flour
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 300 ml milk
  • 2 eggs (whites and yolks separated)
  • 60 g melted butter
  • berries, maple syrup or honey, and powdered sugar

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the dry ingredients. Add the milk, yolks and butter and stir only until combined.

  3. Heat the waffle iron well and grease it lightly.
  4. Pour in batter without overfilling (it puffs up) and cook until golden and crispy, 3 to 5 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  5. Serve right away, stacked, with berries and syrup.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Greek yogurt and fruitCrispy bacon on the sideWhipped cream, on party days
Lili's tipA soft waffle is almost always an iron that wasn't hot enough or batter that was stirred too much. Heat first, stir little.

Koeksisters — Syrupy Spiced Doughnuts

Koeksisters

Cooking20 min
Total50 min

Little spiced dough fritters, fried and soaked in a ginger-and-cinnamon syrup. Sweet, sticky and irresistible.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 300 g flour
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp cinnamon and another tsp of ground ginger
  • 150 ml warm milk (approx.)
  • 300 g sugar and 200 ml water (for the syrup, with fresh ginger and cinnamon)
  • 1 egg, butter, salt, shredded coconut and oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Make the syrup first: boil the sugar, water, ginger and cinnamon for 5 minutes. Let it cool — the syrup must be cold and the fritters hot.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Mix the flour, baking powder, spices and salt. Add the egg, a little butter and the warm milk until you have a soft dough.
  3. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Roll it out to 1 cm thick, cut rectangles, make a slit in the middle and pull one end through it (the classic braided shape, simplified).
  5. Fry in medium oil until well golden.
  6. Drain for a few seconds and dip them right away into the cold syrup. Sprinkle with shredded coconut.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Rooibos tea, like in South AfricaCoffeeAs a sharing dessert, on little plates
Lili's tipThe hot/cold contrast is the trick: a hot fritter in cold syrup drinks up the syrup without falling apart.

Grilled corn with mayo, cheese, lime and a spicy touch — Mexican street food.

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Boil or grill the corn cobs until tender with toasted marks, 10 to 15 minutes, turning them.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  2. Spread each still-hot cob with a thin layer of mayo.
  3. Sprinkle with the cheese, the paprika/chili and salt.
  4. Squeeze lime generously over the top.
  5. Chopped cilantro, and serve right away, with more lime on the side.

🍽️ What to serve it with

As a side dish for tacosAt a barbecue, next to the meatsWith grilled chicken and rice
Lili's tipThe mayo is not there to taste like mayo: it's the 'glue' that holds the cheese and spices to the cob.

Easy Chicken Pozole

Pozole fácil de frango
Prep15 min
Cooking35 min
Total50 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Mexican chicken soup with big corn kernels (hominy), served with cabbage, radish and lime on top.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g chicken (breast or legs)
  • 1 can drained hominy corn (400 g) — or chickpeas, in the backup version
  • 1 onion and 3 garlic cloves
  • 1500 ml chicken broth
  • 1 tsp oregano and another tsp of cumin
  • cabbage in strips, radishes, lime, cilantro and chili, to serve

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Cook the chicken in the broth with half an onion and salt, for 20 minutes. Take it out, shred it and save the broth.
  2. Sauté the other half of the onion and the garlic in a drizzle of oil. Add the strained broth.
  3. Add the hominy, oregano and cumin. Boil for 10 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Boiling too hard breaks delicate ingredients and can curdle sauces with cream or egg. A gentle simmer is almost always enough — and safer.
  4. Return the shredded chicken and cook 5 more minutes. Adjust the salt.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  5. Serve in deep bowls with cabbage, radish, cilantro and lime on top — everyone seasons their own bowl.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Tortillas or totopos (nachos) on the sideDiced avocado on topOn its own — it's a soup-meal
Lili's tipThe raw toppings on top are not decoration: they bring crunch, freshness and acidity to a hot, rich broth.

Chicken Katsu with Rice

Katsu de frango com arroz
Prep15 min
Cooking15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Chicken breaded in panko, crispy and golden, sliced over rice with tonkatsu sauce.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g chicken breasts or boneless thighs
  • 50 g flour
  • 2 beaten eggs
  • 120 g panko (coarse Japanese breadcrumbs)
  • salt, pepper, oil for frying; tonkatsu sauce or mild barbecue sauce; rice and finely shredded cabbage, to serve

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Butterfly the chicken into pieces about 1.5 cm thick. Season with salt and pepper.
  2. Set out three plates: flour, egg and panko. Coat the chicken in that order, pressing the panko on with your hand.
  3. Rest 5 minutes: the coating sticks better and doesn't come off in the oil.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Fry in medium-hot oil for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until well golden and cooked through.
  5. Drain on a rack and rest 3 minutes.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  6. Slice into strips (the classic presentation) and serve over rice, with very fine cabbage and the sauce drizzled over.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Japanese riceMiso soupCabbage salad with sesame and lemon
Lili's tipDon't press the panko with brute force, and don't move it in the skillet during the first 2 minutes: that's how the crust stays whole and crispy.

Dorayaki — Japanese Red Bean Pancakes

Dorayaki
Prep15 min
Cooking15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Two fluffy golden pancakes with a sweet filling in the middle — kids' favorite snack in Japan.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 2 eggs
  • 70 g sugar
  • 1 tbsp honey
  • 130 g flour and 0.5 tsp baking powder
  • 50 ml water or milk
  • 200 g filling: anko (sweet azuki bean paste), Nutella or dulce de leche

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Beat the eggs, sugar and honey until pale and thick.
  2. Add the sifted flour and baking powder and the water. Stir only until combined and rest 15 minutes — the batter thickens and the pancakes get fluffier.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  3. Heat a nonstick skillet over low heat and wipe it with a paper towel with a drop of oil.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  4. Pour in small ladles of batter (8 to 9 cm). When bubbles appear, flip and cook 30 seconds on the other side.
  5. Repeat until the batter is used up, making pairs of the same size.
  6. Spread one pancake with the filling, cover with another and pinch the edges together with your fingers.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Green teaMilk, for the kidsIn a lunch box, like in Japan
Lili's tipLow heat is the secret to the dorayaki's even golden color. High heat makes spots and burns it before it cooks through.

Butter Chicken

Butter chicken
Prep20 min
Cooking25 min
Total45 min
DifficultyMedium
Serves4 people

The creamy cousin of tikka masala: chicken in a tomato, butter and cream sauce, mild and rich.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 600 g chicken, in cubes
  • 150 g yogurt, garlic and ginger (marinade) and 2 tsp garam masala
  • 400 g crushed tomatoes
  • 50 g butter
  • 150 ml heavy cream
  • 1 tsp sugar (balances the tomato)
  • salt, paprika and cilantro

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with garlic, ginger, salt and half of the spices, for 30 minutes or more.💡 Why it matters: Marinating gives salt and spices time to get inside the food — the flavor ends up within, not just on the surface.
  2. Sear the chicken in a hot skillet until it takes on color. Set aside.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  3. In the same skillet, melt the butter, add the tomato, the rest of the spices and the sugar. Cook for 10 minutes until it darkens.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Blend the sauce until completely smooth and return it to the skillet.
  5. Add the cream and the chicken and cook for 8 minutes over low heat.💡 Why it matters: Low heat gives sauces time to thicken and flavors time to come together, without burning the bottom or curdling cream and eggs.
  6. Cilantro on top and serve hot.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Jeera rice or plain basmatiGarlic naanCucumber in yogurt, for freshness
Lili's tipButter chicken should be mild: the heat stays almost invisible. If you want heat, serve chili on the side instead of putting it in the sauce.

Onion Pakoras — Onion Bhaji

Pakoras de cebola
Prep15 min
Cooking15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Indian onion fritters with chickpea flour and spices — crispy and addictive.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 3 large onions, thinly sliced
  • 150 g chickpea flour
  • 1 tsp cumin, another tsp of turmeric, and chili to taste
  • salt, chopped cilantro, water (just a little) and oil for frying

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Salt the onions and squeeze them with your hands for 5 minutes: they release water and soften. That water is what makes the batter.
  2. Add the chickpea flour, the spices and the cilantro and mix. Add water only if it's dry: the batter should coat the onions, not run off.
  3. Heat medium-hot oil.
  4. Fry loose spoonfuls (don't pack the fritters down) for 3 to 4 minutes, until well golden and crispy.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.
  5. Drain on paper towels and add a pinch of salt.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Mint chutney or yogurt sauceChai teaAs a starter for an Indian dinner
Lili's tipLoose fritters fry better: packed mounds stay raw in the middle. Drop them in and don't touch them for the first few minutes.

Lemon Yogurt Cake

Bolo de iogurte e limão
Prep10 min
Cooking35 min
Total45 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves8 people

The easiest cake of all: you measure everything with the yogurt cup, and it always comes out moist.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 8 people
  • 1 cup plain yogurt (125 g) — the cup is the measure
  • 2 cups sugar (measured in the yogurt cup)
  • 3 cups flour
  • 0,5 cup oil
  • 3 eggs
  • 1 lemon (juice and zest) and 1 tbsp baking powder

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Oven at 180°C. Grease a tube pan or a loaf pan.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  2. Mix the yogurt, eggs, sugar and oil until smooth.
  3. Add the lemon zest and juice.
  4. Fold in the flour and baking powder, without beating.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  5. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
  6. If you like, drizzle it while still warm with lemon juice mixed with sugar — it becomes a real lemon cake.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Tea or coffeeBerries on the sideGreek yogurt, for breakfast
Lili's tipThis is the recipe to memorize: 1 yogurt, 2 of sugar, 3 of flour, half of oil, 3 eggs. You'll never need to look it up again.

Passion Fruit Mousse

Mousse de maracujá
Prep10 min
Cooking0 min
Total10 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Three ingredients and ten minutes: the quickest tropical mousse, with just the right tang.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 1 can sweetened condensed milk (397 g)
  • 200 ml heavy whipping cream, very cold
  • 150 ml concentrated passion fruit juice (or pulp with the seeds, strained to taste)
  • pulp of 1 fresh passion fruit, to put on top

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Whip the very cold cream until it is firm.
  2. Mix the condensed milk with the passion fruit juice: you'll see the cream thicken right away — that's the acidity at work.
  3. Fold in the whipped cream with a spatula, in wide movements, so you don't lose the air.💡 Why it matters: Folding gently keeps the air in beaten egg whites and whipped cream — that air is the lightness. Beating hard throws it away.
  4. Pour into bowls and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
  5. Serve with the fresh pulp on top — the crunchy seeds are the perfect contrast.💡 Why it matters: Browning creates brand-new flavor — it's the reaction that gives color and depth. Wet food or a cold pan steams instead of browning, so dry things well and don't crowd the pan.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Butter cookies on the sideAfter spicy dishes — it calms and refreshesWith mint, for the photo
Lili's tipCold, always: warm cream won't whip and the mousse won't set. Bowl and cream straight from the fridge into the mixer.

Apple & Oat Crumble

Crumble de maçã e aveia
Prep15 min
Cooking35 min
Total50 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves6 people

Soft apple and cinnamon underneath, a crispy oat crust on top. Serve it warm, with ice cream.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 6 people
  • 6 apples, peeled and sliced
  • 100 g brown sugar (half for the fruit, half for the crust)
  • 100 g flour
  • 80 g rolled oats
  • 100 g cold butter, in cubes
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • juice of half a lemon and a pinch of salt

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Mix the apples with the lemon juice, half of the sugar and half of the cinnamon. Put them in a baking dish.
  2. With your fingers, rub the cold butter into the flour until it looks like coarse sand.
  3. Add the oats, the rest of the sugar and cinnamon, and the salt. Don't knead: it should stay in lumps.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.
  4. Spread the crust over the fruit without pressing it down.
  5. Oven at 180°C for 30 to 35 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.💡 Why it matters: A hot oven from minute one makes cakes and roasts rise and brown evenly. In a cold oven, the cooking time changes and so does the result.
  6. Rest 10 minutes and serve warm.💡 Why it matters: Resting isn't wasted time: juices redistribute and doughs relax. Cutting or unmolding too early loses liquid, air and texture.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Vanilla ice cream (the classic)Whipped creamGreek yogurt, in the breakfast version
Lili's tipCold butter and big lumps = crispy crust. Melted butter makes a hard lid instead of a crumble.

Watermelon & Mint Smoothie

Smoothie de melancia e hortelã
Prep5 min
Cooking0 min
Total5 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves2 people

The freshest drink of the summer: watermelon, lime and mint blended with ice.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 2 people
  • 400 g seedless watermelon, in cubes
  • 1 lime (the juice)
  • 8 leaves mint
  • 150 g ice
  • a drizzle of honey, only if the watermelon isn't very sweet

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Put the watermelon, lime, mint and ice in the blender.
  2. Blend for 45 seconds, until bright pink and frothy.
  3. Taste before sweetening: ripe watermelon rarely needs honey.💡 Why it matters: Tasting at the end is what separates 'almost good' from 'really good': salt, acidity and heat can be fixed in seconds — but only if you taste.
  4. Serve right away, with a mint leaf on top.

🍽️ What to serve it with

As a snack on hot daysWith badjias or samosas, for a sweet-and-salty snackAfter exercising, to rehydrate
Lili's tipReally do remove all the seeds: blended, they leave bitter specks and ruin the smooth texture.

Quinoa, Mango & Black Bean Salad

Salada de quinoa, manga e feijão preto
Prep15 min
Cooking15 min
Total30 min
DifficultyEasy
Serves4 people

Colorful, fresh and complete: quinoa, beans, mango and lime. A light lunch that keeps well in the fridge.

📸 The process, in photos — and why each step matters

🧺 Ingredients

Serves 4 people
  • 200 g quinoa
  • 1 can cooked black beans, drained (400 g)
  • 1 mango, in cubes
  • 0,5 red onion, finely chopped
  • 1 lime (the juice) and 3 tbsp olive oil
  • cilantro, salt, pepper and avocado (optional)

👩‍🍳 How to make it

  1. Rinse the quinoa and cook it in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until it pops open. Drain and let it cool — a warm salad wilts everything.💡 Why it matters: Cooling before cutting or frosting stops cakes from falling apart and frosting from melting and sliding off. The structure sets outside the oven.
  2. Mix the drained beans, the mango and the onion in a large bowl.💡 Why it matters: Draining well removes extra water or oil — the stuff that softens crusts, thins sauces and makes salads soggy.
  3. Make the dressing: lime juice, olive oil, salt and pepper, well whisked together.
  4. Add the cold quinoa and the dressing and toss.
  5. Cilantro on top. If you use avocado, add it only when serving.

🍽️ What to serve it with

Grilled chicken on top, for a complete mealTortillas or lettuce leaves, to make wrapsOn its own, as a light lunch
Lili's tipWell-drained, cold quinoa is the secret: warm or wet, the salad turns heavy and the dressing runs to the bottom.
